newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 7.0/7.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 7.0/7.5 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended at 7.0/7.5 percent on Friday due to fresh lending by a few banks, dealers said.
The overnight traded as high as 10.0 percent, the level at which it closed on Wednesday.
The money market was closed on Thursday for a Moslem religious holiday.
Earlier, one-month money was at 10.0 percent and three-month at 9.5 percent.
"Some banks came out to lend, probably from funds borrowed earlier from the market," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said though rates were coming off from earlier highs, the market remained short of funds.
"Liquidity is still tight," the dealer said.

Dealers said there was no sign of Bank Negara lending on Friday. The central bank was said to be lending overnight and one-month funds on Wednesday, but only to selected finance and discount houses, dealers said.
The liquidity squeeze followed heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank last week to defend the ringgit from a speculative attack.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers have estimated that between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit was drained from the system.
Dealers said given the continuing pressure on the ringgit, interbank rates were likely to be kept high for the time being.
The ringgit fell to a three-year low of 2.6150/6200 to a dollar in Friday afternoon trade.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were higher across the board due to expectations of softening interbank rates.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up five points to 92.41, or an implied yield of 7.59 percent.
The December contract was up three at 92.65, or 7.35 percent.
